result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A keeps every claim tied to the interviewees: its headline reads '9 of 14 owners' and 64% sits beside '9 of 14 interviewed owners'. Its slide titles state conclusions and support the ask, though it has only 3 presented slides and puts most caveats in the appendix. Answer B covers the limits well, but its headline 'Most independent hardware owners want...' claims market-wide demand. B also inflates the result with an 86% 'use it or consider it' figure and a 'would use it today' headline that drops the register condition, and its slide titles mostly name topics rather than conclusions. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer B's headline ties its claim to the sample ('9 of 14 owners'), its 64% is labelled as 9 of 14 interviewed owners, and every slide title states a conclusion that leads to the build request. Answer A also avoids 'overwhelmingly' and is more open about the limits, but its headline says 'Most independent hardware owners', which claims more than the 14 interviews support. A's '64% / 86%' slide headline also doesn't attach the percentages to the interviewees, and several of its titles only name a topic. B has a smaller wording slip ('More than a third of owners'), and its caveat sits in a caption and an appendix, so it is less prominent than A's.
